netlists.buck:
* Buck converter - lecture Example 2
* Vs = 50 V, D = 0.4, L = 400 uH, C = 100 uF, f = 20 kHz, R = 20 ohm
* Nodes: vs (source +), sw (switch/diode/inductor junction), vo (output), gate (switch drive), 0 (return rail)

* DC source Vs: + at vs, - at the bottom rail
VS vs 0 DC 50

* Switch S between vs and sw, driven by a 0/5 V gate at f = 20 kHz, D = 0.4
* T = 50 us, on-time D*T = 20 us (PW 19.99 us + 10 ns edges); the switch starts ON at t = 0
VG gate 0 PULSE(0 5 0 10n 10n 19.99u 50u)
S1 vs sw gate 0 SWMOD
.model SWMOD SW(Ron=1m Roff=100Meg Vt=2.5 Vh=0)

* Freewheeling diode D: anode on the bottom rail, cathode at sw
D1 0 sw DMOD
* Same junction as CircuitJS's built-in "default" diode (about 0.8 V at 1 A)
.model DMOD D(Is=1.7143528e-7 N=2)

* Output filter and load
L1 sw vo 400u
C1 vo 0 100u
R1 vo 0 20

* Steady state: filter decay time 2RC = 4 ms, so 40 ms is about 10 time constants.
* Max step 0.2 us = 250 points per 50 us period.
.tran 0.2u 40m 0 0.2u
.end
netlists.scr:
* Single-phase half-wave controlled rectifier, R load (lecture Example 5)
* 120 V rms / 60 Hz source, R = 10 ohm, firing angle alpha = 60 deg.
*
* Nodes
*   vs  - source + terminal = thyristor anode
*   vo  - thyristor cathode = top of R (output voltage vo)
*   0   - source - terminal = bottom of R
*   gp  - gate pulse train (control signal only)
*   a1, a2 - internal nodes of the thyristor model
*   cr, ctl - latch logic (raw and filtered switch control)
*
* Thyristor model (no XSPICE, no built-in SCR): a hysteretic voltage-controlled
* switch S1 in series with a near-ideal diode D1 and a 0 V ammeter VIT.
*   - Turn-on : the gate pulse (v(gp) > 2.5 V) closes S1; D1 only lets current
*               flow if the device is forward biased (v_T > 0).
*   - Latch   : while the anode current i(VIT) exceeds the holding current
*               (10 mA) the control stays high, so S1 stays closed after the
*               short gate pulse ends.
*   - Turn-off: when i_T falls below the holding current (i_T -> 0 at wt = pi
*               for an R load) the control drops and S1 opens; D1 blocks any
*               reverse current in the meantime.
*   The 1 us RC (RCT/CCT) between the behavioural source and the switch breaks
*   the algebraic loop i(VIT) -> control -> S1 -> i(VIT), and the switch
*   hysteresis (VT +/- VH) keeps the latch state unambiguous.

.param alpha_deg = 60
.param fsrc = 60
.param tper = {1/fsrc}
.param tdel = {alpha_deg/360/fsrc}

* AC source: vs = Vm sin(wt), Vm = 120*sqrt(2) = 169.7056 V
VS vs 0 SIN(0 169.7056274847714 60 0 0 0)

* Thyristor T1: anode vs, cathode vo
S1 vs a1 ctl 0 SWSCR
D1 a1 a2 DSCR
VIT a2 vo DC 0

* Load
R1 vo 0 10

* Gate pulse train: rises at alpha (2.7778 ms) in every cycle, 0.5 ms wide (~10.8 deg)
VG gp 0 PULSE(0 5 {tdel} 1u 1u 0.5m {tper})

* Latch logic: on if gated OR carrying more than the holding current
BCT cr 0 V = u(v(gp) - 2.5) + u(i(VIT) - 0.01)
RCT cr ctl 1k
CCT ctl 0 1n

* Output power probe (instantaneous p = vo * io)
BPO pout 0 V = v(vo) * i(VIT)

* Near-ideal switch and diode (forward drop ~0.06 V at 15 A)
.model SWSCR SW(VT=0.5 VH=0.1 RON=1m ROFF=1G)
.model DSCR D(IS=1n N=0.1 RS=1m)
* For a realistic ~1 V thyristor drop, swap in instead:
* .model DSCR D(IS=1e-12 N=1.5 RS=5m)

.tran 10u 100m 0 10u

* Steady-state measurements over exactly 3 cycles (50 ms .. 100 ms)
.meas tran vo_avg AVG v(vo) from=50m to=100m
.meas tran vo_rms RMS v(vo) from=50m to=100m
.meas tran io_avg AVG i(VIT) from=50m to=100m
.meas tran io_rms RMS i(VIT) from=50m to=100m
.meas tran vs_rms RMS v(vs) from=50m to=100m
.meas tran p_out AVG v(pout) from=50m to=100m
.meas tran pf param='p_out/(vs_rms*io_rms)'

.end
netlists.ce-amp:
* CE amplifier, fixed bias, bypassed emitter -- lecture figure (i): +20 V, beta = 50
* Nodes: vcc (supply), vi (source), b (base), c (collector), e (emitter), vo (output)
*
* Model: BF = 50 (figure). IS = 3.5e-15 chosen so VBE = Vt*ln(IC/IS) = 0.700 V at
* IC ~ 2.0 mA (27 C, Vt = 25.865 mV). Early effect off (VAF not set = infinite), BR = 1,
* no junction capacitances.
*
* Source: 2 mV peak, 10 kHz (mid-band: at 1 kHz the 40 uF bypass is only ~3x above its
* ~320 Hz pole and |Av| drops to ~147). No UIC: the .tran starts from the DC operating
* point, so every coupling/bypass capacitor is already charged -- no settling time needed.

VCC    vcc 0   DC 20
VI     vi  0   DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 2m 10k)

C1     vi  b   10u
RB     vcc b   430k
RC     vcc c   2k
Q1     c   b   e   QNPN
RE     e   0   1k
CE     e   0   40u
C2     c   vo  10u
* vo is an open terminal in the figure; 10 Meg gives the node a DC path (negligible load)
RPROBE vo  0   10Meg

.model QNPN NPN(IS=3.5e-15 BF=50)

.op
.tran 0.2u 1m 0 0.2u
.ac dec 20 10 1Meg

.meas tran vipp PP v(vi) from=0.5m to=1m
.meas tran vopp PP v(vo) from=0.5m to=1m
.meas tran av_tran param='vopp/vipp'
.meas ac av_mid FIND vm(vo) AT=10k
.meas ac av_1k FIND vm(vo) AT=1k

.end
